title: Bram and the Ledger
premise: Gideon Galloway, a night-shift dispatcher who has quietly solved three deaths the police dismissed as accidents, is drawn into the disappearance of a young accountant named Vera Ostrander when her diary arrives at his dispatch office—still being written, weeks after she vanished. Following entries that reference a coded ledger hidden in the taxi company's own fare records, Gideon realizes Vera discovered the company's owner was laundering money through phantom routes, and that someone inside his small found family of night workers may have helped make her disappear. As the diary's final pages close in on a name, Gideon must choose between protecting the people he loves and exposing the truth, ultimately confronting the killer in the depot's garage and using the ledger itself to force a confession. In the end, Vera is found alive in hiding, the ledger goes to the police, and Gideon—no longer invisible—accepts that belonging means letting others see him.
about_author: Ansel Fairweather is the pen name of a former municipal records clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's paperwork and believes every mystery hides in an ordinary document. They write quiet, procedural mysteries about overlooked people who notice too much.

chapters.title: The Night Frequency
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. On a slow Tuesday shift, Gideon introduces his world—the dispatch office, the drivers who treat the depot like home, and his private habit of solving what the police won't. A package arrives addressed to no one: Vera Ostrander's diary, its last entry dated nine days after her disappearance. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the invisible man noticed.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Reading the diary, Gideon maps Vera's last weeks: a meticulous junior accountant who grew frightened of the fare ledgers she audited. The post-disappearance entries are terse, coded, and terrified—written by someone hiding, or someone performing. He visits her apartment and finds it staged, too tidy. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Phantom Routes
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Cross-referencing the diary against dispatch records, Gideon finds dozens of fares for cabs that never left the garage—money moving through the company like blood. His boss, Marisol, catches him at the terminal and warns him off with something close to fear. Emotional beat: the discovery that rot lives inside his sanctuary.

chapters.title: The People Who Keep the Lights On
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Gideon and driver Ray Okonkwo. A warm interlude: diner breakfast with the night crew, establishing the found family—Ray, dispatcher-in-training Priya, mechanic Sal. But Gideon notices each of them deflects when Vera's name surfaces. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by suspicion; loyalty beginning to cost.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Gideon confronts Marisol gently; she admits Vera came to her a week before vanishing, asking about the phantom routes, and that Marisol told the owner, Dale Voss, to cover for her staff. She swears she never meant harm. Emotional beat: guilt and the first fracture in trust—truth vs. protection made personal.

chapters.title: A Cipher of Fares
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Decoding the diary's numbers against the ledger, Gideon realizes Vera hid the real accounts inside fake trip logs—a map only a dispatcher could read. The trail points to a storage unit and to someone with after-hours access codes. Only four people have them. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling as the suspect list becomes his family.

chapters.title: Sal's Quiet Hands
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Evidence tightens on Sal, whose debts and access fit perfectly—and whose alibi checks out just a little too neatly. Gideon tails him, witnesses a dead drop, and is spotted. That night someone ransacks the dispatch office and takes the diary. Emotional beat: paranoia; the hunter realizing he is also hunted.

chapters.title: The Trap We Build Together
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon, with Priya. Refusing to go to police without proof, Gideon confides in Priya and they set a trap: a forged ledger page planted where the thief will look. The bait is taken—but by Ray, not Sal, acting under threat to his family. Emotional beat: heartbreak; loyalty weaponized, and Gideon's certainty shaken.

chapters.title: Bay Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Following Ray's coerced errand to the depot garage, Gideon walks into Voss's ambush and learns the truth: Voss killed the auditor before Vera, faked her death, and kept her writing the diary under duress to find her own cipher. Bay Nine becomes a standoff; Gideon uses the ledger's final entry—Voss's own signature on a phantom route—to buy seconds until Ray and Marisol arrive. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into courage; the invisible man standing in full light.

chapters.title: First Fare of the Morning
chapters.summary: POV: Gideon. Aftermath: Voss arrested, Vera found alive in a safehouse she'd engineered from her own coded entries, the ledger with the detectives. The night crew gathers at the diner, awkward and changed, learning to be seen. Gideon takes the first dispatch call of the morning and answers it with his real name. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging chosen, not hidden.
